bearings.paper_claim: Stance is tracked as a trajectory over 28-day snapshots, with embedding persistence so silent users keep a stance. Movement is sorted into seven dynamics using a static band of median plus MAD. Mirror-image O-to-S and S-to-O flip curves suggest external events. Users with no direct stance are predicted through graph propagation over their neighbours.
bearings.system_side: Module docstring (lines 3-21) states the transplant. Code confirms 91-day default windows (line 26), last observed stance carried through silent windows (lines 48-55), the seven-dynamics classifier (lines 64-67), flip curves (lines 72-84), cosponsor and HCoI co-movement (lines 94-120), and CSV-only imputation proposals that leave the matrix untouched (lines 132-151). Re-run on the press CSV in scratch: 2,388 rows, 373 members, 18 windows.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The design vocabulary transfers. The paper says the mirror symmetry suggests external events; it does not establish an event detector the module can rely on. The paper's neighbour inference is GNN message passing over learned embeddings, not a copy rule, so the system's neighbour-based imputation is an analogue only.
bearings.verifier_note: Trajectory framing, persistence, the seven dynamics and mirror curves are all in the paper text. Softened wording: the paper says the mirror symmetry suggests external events, and that unlabelled users get predictions from graph structure rather than explicit neighbour inference. The module matches its description. The static-band and imputation points are handled in bearings 2 and 4.

bearings.paper_claim: The median plus MAD static band is applied to continuous stance values p in [-1,1] from the MLP, computed over all users' absolute changes. The paper gives no condition that users must post in nearly every period; its 10-tweet filter only implies about one interaction per snapshot on average.
bearings.system_side: Band is computed on observed-to-observed transitions only, from confidence-weighted means of stance_sign in {-1,0,+1}, floored at 0.05 (code lines 56-63). Live static_band 0.7076 is reproduced. Of 2,989 transitions, 2,737 (91.6 percent) are static and 252 move: S-to-O 111, O-to-S 43, S-to-MS 88 (a move with no sign change), S-to-LS 7, O-to-LO 2, O-to-MO 1 (flip_curves in stance_dynamics.json, matching the scratch re-run).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The band means what the paper intends only where stance is continuous and densely observed. With pooled quarterly signs it mainly measures how coarse the labels are. The paper gives no support for the seven-class counts. The within-side classes are rare because a move must exceed about 0.71 on a [-1,1] scale; they are not empty by construction.
bearings.verifier_note: The band value and the 91.6 percent static share reproduce. The rel claim that only near-sign reversals register as movement is wrong: S-to-MS (88, no sign change) is the second-largest moving class after S-to-O (111). The claim that the paper's band presumes users who post in nearly every period is not in the paper.

bearings.paper_claim: Neighbour co-movement: users shift in the same direction as their 1-hop and 2-hop neighbours (diagonal dominance in Fig. 6). The authors describe tight-knit communities moving together, call it a descriptive correlation, and report no null model and no identification. The text gives no numbers; values appear only in the heatmaps.
bearings.system_side: Co-movement counts same versus opposite direction for neighbours who both move in a window. Diagonal dominance is declared above 0.55 (code line 106). Cosponsor result as stored: same 134, opposite 122, 52.3 percent, below threshold, so null. The HCoI figure of 49 percent cited in the rel is not stored in stance_dynamics.json. Scratch re-run on the current press_hcoi.json gives same 302, opposite 296, 50.5 percent, also below threshold. No permutation or common-shock control exists.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's result is a descriptive correlation at 28-day resolution on Twitter, not evidence of influence. Do not carry the paper's potential social influences wording or its asymmetric social influence signals claim into system text. A null on one layer is a null on that layer only.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper text verified, including the no-null-model caveat. The cosponsor figure reproduces from the stored JSON. The 49 percent HCoI figure does not reproduce (50.5 percent on the current community file), so cite the reproduced value or mark the earlier figure UNVERIFIED. Both values are null under the ad hoc 0.55 rule.

bearings.paper_claim: Silent-user inference is validated with 5-fold cross-validation over annotated users. For validation users, all edges to referendum-labelled hashtags are removed before training and inference. Scoring is macro-F1 per period on that period's validation users, chosen over accuracy because of class imbalance. Reported TWLGCN levels are steady between 70 and 90 percent.
bearings.system_side: Imputation takes the mean tier score of at least 5 cosponsor neighbours (MINNB=5, line 132) and keeps blank member-issue cells with |est| at least 0.75 (CONF, line 132). Masking check compares the neighbour estimate sign with the known label sign on confident cells only: 77.5 percent on n=1,087 (stance_dynamics.json). Proposals: 307 (CSV has 308 lines including header). True Neutral (score 0) counts as a negative sign (line 143). The final print says at least 3 informative neighbors while the threshold is 5 (line 152). No party-only or majority-class baseline, no macro-F1, no retraining, no 5-fold split.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's protocol retrains a model with masked own-edges and reports macro-F1 across folds. The system's check is a neighbour-only estimate scored by raw sign agreement on a confidence-selected subset. Call it an analogue. The 77.5 percent is not comparable to the paper's macro-F1 range and stays UNVERIFIED (DE-062) until a party or majority baseline is run.
bearings.verifier_note: The paper protocol is stated accurately. The code comment calling the check 'their protocol' overstates the match. The bearing omitted that the 77.5 percent is conditioned on |est| at least 0.75, which is added here.

bearings.paper_claim: Carrying learned embeddings and MLP weights forward between snapshots beats re-initialising each period, by 1.3 to 9.8 percent on Exit_DS. The 28-day window was chosen by a sensitivity analysis on giant-component fraction: shorter windows fragment the graph and longer ones mask rapid shifts.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 3.3 p.5 (sensitivity in Fig. S2, supplement); Sec. 4.3.1 p.10
bearings.system_side: Persistence carries the last observed raw stance into silent windows (lines 48-55), not learned embeddings. Carried windows also enter transition counts (lines 69-73), which inflates static counts and credits flips to the window where posting resumes. The 91-day default (line 26) is justified by an analogy comment about quarters, with no sensitivity run.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's persistence gain is for warm-started learned representations that keep updating from new edges. It does not support freezing a categorical label. The window rule can be borrowed, but it needs per-window graphs the press corpus does not supply. Fig. S2 is in the supplement and was not checked.
bearings.verifier_note: Checked in Sec. 3.3 and 4.3.1. The paper validates embedding carry-over and a 28-day window with a sensitivity check. It does not validate label carry-forward, the 91-day window, or the system's imputation. The system-side description matches the code.

bearings.paper_claim: Active per-period user-user edges (mentions, quotes and replies, given as examples) add about 3 percent macro-F1 on both datasets. Passive follower or friend edges add little, and combining both does not help. The paper's Act graph is directed from the initiating user to the target.
bearings.system_side: The social interaction layer uses reposts (weight 1.0) and mentions (0.4), normalised by the author's post volume with a floor of 25, and capped at 0.25 per pair. Its output is symmetric (mean of both directions), not directed. Reposts, the layer's strongest edge, are not among the paper's Act edge types. stance_dynamics tests co-movement and imputation only on the cosponsor and HCoI layers, never on this layer.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's evidence is that interaction edges help stance inference, not that they carry influence. Member accounts post far less than the paper's users, so expect sparser edges. Any test belongs in the descriptive lane. The layer's author-volume normalisation is a separate choice that this paper does not validate, and it must not be cited as support for the rejected per-edge volume normalisation.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claim verified. The rel's system-side claim of a directed layer is wrong: the output is symmetric. The paper's Act list does not contain reposts.

related.why: Item exists. The HCoI acronym matches its hidden communities of interest method, so the link to the HCoI layer is plausible. This is a system-side link; the Zhou paper does not cite it.
Item exists (Twitter As Data). Relevant to the Twitter measurement issues behind hashtag-proxy labels. The July 2026 provenance claim in the rel was not checked.

Item text is the paper Comparing Fine-Tuned RoBERTa with Traditional ML Models for Stance Detection in Political Tweets, so the rel rationale holds. The item ext title (Roman Urdu) is a stale mismatch and should be corrected in the item.
Item exists and its title matches (LLM-enhanced logic tensor network for stance detection). The Zhou paper lists LLM-based user-level stance as future work (Sec. 6.1 p.17), which is accurate.

Item exists. The paper concedes a non-representative Santiago news-follower sample (Sec. 3.2, Sec. 5.1 p.12, Sec. 6.1 p.16), and Hargittai is relevant to such biases. The paper does not cite her, so 'explains' should read 'relevant to'.

Item exists (influence maximization with graph embedding and GNN). Both use graph embeddings on social graphs, but Kumar addresses seed selection and the Zhou paper addresses stance classification, so same-method overstates the link.

summary_issues: The summary says the paper's gains come from a GNN trained on dense tweet data. The paper describes its user-hashtag matrices as sparse per 28-day window (Sec. 3.6 p.10; Sec. 6 p.15). Replace dense with sparse.
The summary's account of Paul's note (his component position, and that he wants change-likelihood modelling) is not in the item: paul_entries holds only a bare link and no takeaways. Unverified here.
The summary's 77.5 percent sign agreement is reported without its condition: it covers only cells with |est| at least 0.75 (stance_dynamics.py line 142). It is also not a macro-F1 figure.

The 49 percent HCoI co-movement figure the summary relies on is not stored in data/stance/stance_dynamics.json. A scratch re-run on the current press_hcoi.json gives 50.5 percent (302 same, 296 opposite). Both values are null under the 0.55 rule.

The summary's claim that the paper's band and window are unvalidated is accurate. The summary should also note the paper's abstract says 20 monthly periods, but its periods are 28 days (11 plus 9, Sec. 3.3 p.5). Do not carry monthly into system text.

Summary figures checked and correct: 1.21M tweets, 80 and 106 labelled hashtags, kappa 0.81 to 0.94 on 100 snapshots per dataset, 1.3 to 9.8 percent persistence gain, about 3 percent Act gain, 134 versus 122 co-movement, 307 proposals, static band 0.708 with about 92 percent static share.
